I'm looking to gather the playerbase's knowledge/opinions on the current meta fleets and their counters. My main goal is to make a diagram that will help new players (and maybe myself) better understand making good comps, but also want to get at potential balance issues (e.g. does fleet X truly have no counters?), and at the nature of strong all-ins that an enemy isn't prepared for (e.g. 40 rocket shuttles, 12 CLs, etc).

Please indulge me in this little project and respond to this thread with something like:

**Fleet Archetype** 
The type of fleet, description, potentially a fleet file as an example. If you really want to help, provide a screenshot of one of the main ships
**Why it's powerful**
Description of how it's played out in matches (including information about who was in the match can help, e.g. skill level, but I don't intend to restrict this in any way), what specific fleets it killed/won against, any weaknesses it had, etc
**Strategies for countering it**
List strategies you or others have tried for countering it in real games, and how effective they were. Then, feel free to list strategies you think should work, but haven't been tried yet. 
Please list at least one 3k (or 12k comp) that counters it
**Balance changes it's affected by**
Have there been any PTB changes that make the fleet more powerful? Less powerful? Any hypothetical changes that would affect this?

The goal is to make something like this: https://i.redd.it/zfqhu451s6931.jpg , so please list out specific well-known fleet archetypes. Of course, player skill is a factor, but I intend to visualize the skill-range outcome in some way, e.g. evenly matched fleets vs fleets where the comp/build gives an edge.
Does this only refer to fleets newly powerful on PTB or affected by the PTB? Or is this anything that's good on PTB or live?

As an example:

**Fleet Archetype**
Frigate blob, e.g. 5 frigates armed with 120mm or 250mm guns supported by corvettes mounting PD, softkill, and EWAR
**Why it's powerful**
Frigate blobs have high mobility, high DPS, and strong jamming / low radar signature. They also have strong PD (especially against craft), and generally have omnisoftkill suites. This fleet is often countered by monitors, but is very effective against soft OSP targets, like liners, tugs, and shuttles. 
**Strategies for countering it**
A nuanced discussion (had its own thread), but common counters for frigblob are:
- monitors, especially in places they can control a large portion of the map with bombshell, or with mobility buffs from drives. Monitors struggle with mobility/full map presence, and can be focused down if facing a frigate ball 1:1 without supporting sensor assets or if ambushed.
- Ocellos, for their ability to bring floodlights and break jamming and providing locks, and decent damage of 450 against frigates. Ocellos can die to frigblobs when shot from side-angles, so need to be supported by other assets with good DPS and need to be range/position controlled. 
- LRT/EWAR: essential tools for gaining and maintaining tracks, can require multiple offsets
- 250 liners, when supported. A single 250 salvo can kill a frigate or two, but needs to be carefully range controlled and supported by the team to get shots on target without dying to 120mm HE
- 450 liners, essential for high-DPS long range supporting fire
- cruise missiles, e.g. massed S2s or containers. While frigate blobs have strong PD, they are often grouped in a way that makes it difficult to softkill missiles against all of the ships from all angles, so containers can often get through, especially if their PD or softkill has been degraded
**Balance Changes it's affected by**
Changes to craft G have made RPF more effective against craft, making frigblob difficult to strike as a carrier player. New PTB changes introduce tools that make it significantly easier to counter blobs, namely MD-fragmentation munitions and buffed EWR/LRT tracking

**Massed beam DD cap fleet**
Fleet containing at least 4 really cheap beamstones, aided by equally cheap gunvettes and cringe cappers. Typically 4 beamstones + 6 sprinters
**Why it is powerful**
Large amount of beams allows you to disperse them in critical points around a map and severely punish enemy ships of all sizes once they decide to push. Beam DDs remain hidden until the last moment, they are guided by tracks generated by your sprinters and the rest of your team. Cheap corvettes can be thrown onto points, but they rely on the beamstones for combating contesting enemy cappers and keeping points from being recaptured. Once you gain point advantage, its really hard for the enemy to push unless beamstones are delt with first.
**Counters**
Due to beamstones being cringed and not very good hull in general its easy for light assets, like shuttles or tugs, to outflank them and either evade or outrange their beam. CMD missiles and craft are great at dealing with assets without substantial hardkill. Its useful to have sensor assets for detecting hidden DDs, but its often easy to guess their position based on terrain and point layout of the map. Cheap containers are also good at supressing beams without PD, but they are not reliable. Lastly, if the position of a beamstone is known, its often possible for high DPS frontline to disable the beam before it manages to make an impact.
**Balance Changes it's affected by**
OSP get new toys to fight sprinters (MD frag, 250 bomb), which make it more difficult for such fleet to execute 1st part of its victory plan, which is relying on getting early point advantage by capping with cringed throw-away sprinters.

**Fleet Archetype**
Capture fleet, 5+ sprinters or shuttles with minimal investment, sometimes supported by 'harder' assets such as frigates, destroyers, monitors, etc.

**Why it's powerful**
Capture fleets have poor damage output but are virtually essential for winning on any map running control points, as they can spend relatively few points to contest and win capture points while also having many opportunities to attempt recapture. Despite their low combat power, most games where one team lacks a cap fleet are a defacto loss for said team.
 
**Strategies for countering it**
Capture fleets consisting of only light assets are trivially easy to counter, posing nearly no combat threat when directly encountered. Of course, some strategies work better against them than others:

- Carriers, generally, are extremely effective against caps due to craft and their inherent ability to loiter.
- Missile fleets are able to stop cap fleets without physically moving assets anywhere near them.
- Direct frontline assets will typically win against cappers.
- Midline assets will, as well, usually win against cappers with little contest.

**Balance Changes it's affected by**
Any change which makes very light assets more vulnerable will hit cappers: the at-this-time recent PTB testing mass drivers as an area denial tool is an example. This also means many anti-blob tools have a knock-on effect of being effective against capture assets as well.

lemme find the 5 month old write up I did on the different ASF investment of ANS carrier archetypes

> So: [ANS carrier] anti-craft fighter investments. There are [three] approaches. Assuming you make any investment at all, as Star pointed out. 
> 
> The first is TaistyCookie's method of the minimum viable fighter escort required to get bombers through an enemy CVLN. This wants at least 12 ceramic bombers and 32 basic fighters split 50/50 between 20mm and coilgun (10 pts and 17 pts respectively, can be even cheaper if you drop the hico), with a sprinkling of S1 ACMs. You use the ceramic bombers to tank the BVR engagement, then mop up with the fighters. Repeat until you get strikes through. The high craft requirement for this cheapest investment means you can't run it in a single levy fleet. The closest you can get is a 4 hangar levy, which can only bring 8 of the desired 12 bombers.
> 
> The 2nd is Falk Tethy's method of matching the SDM-2 cycle rate of the Moorline, using Hunter's Ceramic SDM-2 bomber tech (Meat Weasel). This requires 3-4 ceramic SDM-2 bombers to act as heavy fighters, microed specifically with doctrines set to focus and salvo size 1, firing cmd only SDM-2. Manually click each target to engage with them, and tank all return fire. You still need ~16 fighters to make up the rest of the SDM-2 cycle rate, but you won't be able to afford many munitions here so keep them cheap.
> 
> In both of the first two approaches, the goal isn't to fully contest the air war. You just need to ball up a small squad of fighters to protect a bomber group, with the fighters buying enough time to get the bomber group to the target (and hopefully back).
> 
> The 3rd is SAH Spamto. You bring 2 levys full of centerline fuel tank/S1 bay tantos with a mix of 20mm, coil, and nose illum. Then you send your 84 tantos to assassinate the enemy backline, and after that their LNs. In none of these do you use gucci high investment fighters. Since it can match fighter spam CVLN's pt for pt, frame for frame, it can contest them anywhere and everywhere.

**Fleet Archetype**
Shadow Wizard Money Gang (SWMG), or S3 bomber-maxed double Levy 
**Why it's powerful**
You ball up bombers and then you right click on targets. The targets die. Use your bombers for scouting or to drain enemy point defense/missile networks afterwards, as bringing them back to land clogs up your cycle speed and therefor your DPM. Bomber decoys allow for PD pen with minimal effort. The Ceramic, Ablative, and Hico craft modules are all very useful in preventing enemy missile based anti-craft investment from mattering.
**Strategies for countering it**
In addition to the normal things that apply to every carrier, like ship based ACM investment; having good sensor coverage and any fighters in the area makes it very easy to zone attacks out and pick off bombers. This includes things like backpack fighters off frontline fleets.
**Balance changes it's affected by**
On current main branch, this fleet struggles more than it used to as it can no longer use ceramic to defend against SDM-2 fire, nor can it use bomber based SDM-2s to defend itself from enemy craft. On PTB, this fleet requires significantly more effort to play than before, as you can no longer int your bombers directly at the target over open space as soon as they come off the carrier deck without taking losses. Careful pathing to utilize cover and avoid enemy sensors is necessary to get good results. Accordingly, don't put up more wings of craft in the air than you can micro at any one time, lest you lose them when you aren't looking.

**Fleet Archetype**
Kitty Petter, or S2 bomber-maxed single Levy. So named because you can play it one handed while you pet your cat.
As S2 based loadouts are significantly more expensive than torpedo based ones, the Kitty Petter archetype utilizes a single invested Levy, as it cannot afford to buy two hulls without seriously cutting into mag depth. 
**Why it's powerful**
Unlike the above fleet, a Kitty Petter Levy drops its munitions at long ranges to avoid any form of enemy counterplay. Bomber decoys allow for PD pen with minimal effort. While Ceramic, Ablative, and Hico craft modules remain useful, what really shines in contested environments with this fleet is Stealth coating. This, paired with the long range of S2 strikes, brings your already small exposure time to enemy sensors (and thus counterplay) to ludicrously low levels, or even no time spent detected at all. For these reasons, it is incredibly easy to play, if not always the most points efficient option, even against significantly better players.
**Strategies for countering it**
As ship based defenses are almost entirely ignored, countering this requires a very on-the-ball CVLN player. They need not just extremely excellent sensor coverage, but many widely dispersed interceptors in position to stop the S2 drop.
**Balance changes it's affected by**
On current main branch, this fleet struggles *slightly* more than it used to as it can no longer use bomber based SDM-2s to defend itself from enemy craft. This fleet is mostly unaffected by PTB craft maneuver changes, remaining effective even when played with one hand.
Bombers needing to pay for command channels and this being incompatible with the bomber decoy launcher has led to a split in kitty petter builds; either they upgrade to slightly pricier Act!/[EO] and continue to use the decoy launcher, or they continue to use the cmd/backup seekers and add jamming and decoy penaids to the salvo

**Fleet Archetype** 
Journeyman Half-cap "Jcaps", e.g 1200-1500pt Journeyman CVL equipped for light ASF and strike duties, combined with as many 2xT20 chaffbox shuttles you can fit in the remainder. (or whatever other capping assets you may so desire)
**Why it's powerful**
Since CVs are one of the more powerful anti-capfleet tools, being able to bring craft-based light strike to bear on enemy capping assets allows for significant overmatch when contesting points. It also provides the opportunity to stop an enemy CV, whether full 3K or another CV-halfcap, from doing the same to your cappers by contesting the airspace around objectives. Bonus points for having a single sortie of anti-capital strike to land an opportunistic finishing blow to swing the frontline engagement. Also very good at rooting out beam DDs to clear the way for your cappers.
**Strategies for countering it**
Token ACM investment on opfor frontline seriously hampers the ability of Jcaps' to operate, as you dont have the craft numbers to sustain losses and the only way you find out about ACMs is by getting a wing killed by them. Another potential way of countering this fleet is by having 5K of Levys and 3K of CLs hellpush E side Gold Rush and kill you. All in all, you have less cappers than a full cap fleet and you have less craft than a full CV one, so expect an uphill battle if either (or both) of those archetypes are brought in full by the enemy composition. Lastly, since Jcaps craft prey on minimally defended assets like sprinters or DDs, a lack of those assets in the enemy team limits the impact the Jman can have.
**Balance changes it's affected by**
The PTB craft maneuver nerfs affect this greatly, as RPF even in low quantities can attrit your wings of craft, as well as sarissas currently being a death sentence for any wings in the AO. The changes to shift ASF engagements to S1 missiles by removing SDM2 on craft and nerfing guns have made fighting an uphill ASF battle much more achievable.

Very basic entry level overview of CL archetypes for someone else to crib off, since I've played around with all of them but not well enough to write one of these I think. Each of these fleets are better on PTB than on Main branch, due to the CLN and craft evasion changes reducing the power of their main backline counters.

3CL: maximum 250mm firepower, typically with the best point defense, damage control, and softkill of the three.
2CL Caps: The same as the above, but cuts 1 CL to buy 5-6 cappers depending on investment. Can also reduce this to 3 cringe cappers to buy a single BDD.
2CL w/ Ocello Killers: Cuts 1 CL to buy 12 Ocello Killer S3H hybrids. Depending on tuning and optimal encounters, these can theoretically kill anywhere from 2 (6 rounds per) to 4 Ocellos (3 rounds per in perfect conditions using Ares tuning), or to structure break 2 Liners if the hits are broadside on (potentially killing 4 Liners if the hits are bow to stern, so some of these tunings are cruise TRP capable). 
3CL w/ Liner Killers: The newest of the bunch. Reduces DC and point defense investments (also typically goes from 4 to 3 AE per CL) to buy 9 rounds of S3H, 3 per ship. These can be used to full kill one Liner or Ocello, or to help kill 3 separate Liners faster if fired from a single ship instead of the full formation.

Some combination of these fleets has made for excellent all-in comps since at least carriers release update, as they are among the most resistant to craft of any ANS ship type, especially when multiple of these fleets are on the field

Some of the main counters to CLs:
- ocellos, usually a hard counter in a 1v1 since they outrange you and outarmor you unless you are able to get an ambush or side shot
- 450 liners beyond 8km with offset LRT or ocello lock
- monitors if within plasma range and the cls cant disengage
- cln / s2 spam if the cls fail softkill

### Fleet Archetype

Barracuda maxed Moorline with R2 strike focus.
Backline with its own sensor support from wake / radar skiffs
Hardkill, SMD and ASF check.

### Why it's powerful

With the amount of Cudas a Moorline can bring any normal SMD investment from ANS leads to the Moorline having a lot more Cudas than ANS has SMDs.
R2 from large flights need massed hardkill to be defeated, impossible to achieve with cappers or single Beamstones.
To kill them before they launch options are: SMDs (expensive, limited), AMMs (limited, short range), Sarissa (expensive and power hungry, limiting drives), Auroras (bad for most other threats ANS faces, see CLN + same problems as the Sarissa).
Can ignore small SMD or AMM/ACM investment as losing a few craft is only a slight annoyance. 
R2 have a short arm time. R2 can even knock out a BB through active hardkill and remove its armor (two deck cycles, for example, give 48 R2s). 
Below critical mass RPF just turns all craft yellow or orange and will struggle to kill.

### Strategies for countering it

The R2 Cudas often come completely unarmed (sometimes even without 20mm to save on arming time), even a token fighter force with missiles can rack up lots of kills.
R2 Cudas need escort wings vs craft, winning the ASF war stops the R2 attacks.
R2 block fuel slots, when turning around most flights will be near their fuel limit, or even out of fuel. Catching them in a dogfight is free kills. 
Above critical mass RPF causes entire flights to get wiped. 
Large Cuda swarms are easy to spot, 250 RPF from CLs can cause massive losses.
The constant stream of starting and landing Cudas is a great way to lead sprinter bombers ( or a cruise strike) to the CLN.

### Balance Changes it's affected by
Craft evasion nerf: Lower critical RPF mass.
Sarissas become a no fly zone.
Cheap SSMs with the 3pip frag breakpoint and SDM2 removal from craft lets cudas outrange most Tanto builds using 1 point missiles.

**4tc Spyglass BB**
Solomon fitted with 450 mm guns as main battery, and Spyglass radar buffed by 4 track correlators. Can be used as a single hull fleet with missile complement, or run with cappers/support ships. Usually carries full softkill and ACMs to defend against strikes.
**Why its powerfull**
Spyglass radar generates tracks up to maximum range of 450 mm guns, which makes 4tc BB able to fight back against any other 450mm equipped ship on OSP, negating sensor range advantage of LRT. It can punish any ship larger than a tug up to 11 km away, often denying multiple points at once from being conested by larger hulls if its positioned well. Especially good against liners since they are easiest to hit at long range.
**Counters**
- Ocellos - even tho BB can stand up quite well to enemy 450 mm fire, properely built, dodging ocellos can eventually supress a battleship, since they can avoid most of the dmg due to more thrust and slimmer profile.
- Ambush tactics - Battleships are usually ill suited for fighting smaller hulls, and even if they have pickets or anti-light missiles its often possible to drive up to it with a pair of rocket shuttles or a torp tug. It reqires smart use of terrain to hide approach.
- Rails/MDs - they outrange 450 mm guns and even tho they cant kill, they degrade BBs ability to dodge and make it vounerable to 450 mm fire.
- Massed missiles/craft - even tho BB can carry full softkill and quite a lot of ACMs, when its degraded or out of position its vounerable to missile strikes, which means the end for such BB. After a strike a gun/bomb followup is needed to finish the job.
- Jamming - Spyglass radar is easy to jam once you get within 10 km of it. Monitor fleet equipped with jammers can cover its approach through open space untill BB is in range of plasma and 250/100 mm guns. Risky tactic, since there are often other ships providing offset tracks for BB.  Solomon can also sometimes carry second radar and illum for anti jam

**Balance changes**
SDM-2 nerf means its more expensive to defend against bombers, might reqiure BB to rely on S3H ACMs for anti-bomber duties

Ok, I did say I would do a writeup about torpcorvs at some point, so here it goes.

**Fleet Archetype: Torpcorv-based capfleet**
Because they are made of numerous, individually-cheap ships, capfleet archetypes are less rigid than most others. A Torpcorv-based capfleet refers to one in which VLS-3 armed corvettes are expected to do most of the work of infiltrating enemy caps and defending friendly ones.
The most standard torpcorv fleets would look like this:
- A singular beam DD, required for denying the center point on 1-neutral maps
- 2 sensor assets (ELINT or spyglass), to compensate for the mediocre radar on the eponymous corvettes
- 3-5 corvettes, run individually, typically loaded with a mk61, defender, VLS1, and VLS3 filled with a mix of torpedos and hybrids
- 0-3 gun or cringe cappers, used in much the same manner as they are today
Like in modern capfleets, some ships could be swapped out for orbital bombers or a gun vauxhall, though flexibility was somewhat lower due to the higher base cost of a torpedo corvette.
**Why it was powerful**
When played well, torpcorvs could defeat practically any OSP clipper, including gun shuttles, rocket shuttles, and MMTs. This made them a self-sufficient and cost-efficient way to fight OSP capfleets relying on the aforementioned builds.
**Strategies for countering it**
MMTs are at worst an even matchup against torpcorvs, and rocket shuttles can also destroy them under favorable circumstances. Additionally, they struggle against larger ships such as monitors and liners. 
**Balance changes it's affected by**
Too many to count, but this build was harmed significantly by the introduction of carriers, which torpcorvs were largely defenseless against.
Simultaneously, the meta evolved towards overmatch-style capfleets, which torpcorvs were mostly ineffective against. These days, they tend to be a rare sight.

Instead of dispersing the torpcorvs across the map where they are individually vulnerable and prone to being picked off by anything and everything, you ball them up in a blob where they can specialize mounts to provide mutual support to the formation as a whole. Deploy nearby allied frontline, so they can finish off your targets.

Common fleet on both sides of the barricade. On AN it can consist of a capital ship with 450 mm guns aided by rail DDs, or 450 mm CH + rail CH. On OSP its most commonly encountered in form of 450 mm CC + rail CC, sometimes with 450 mm LN in place of Ocello. In case of OSP often aided by LRT sensor.
**Advantages**
Rails are great force multiplier for 450 mm guns, they hit moving targets reliably at long range and cause fires that overwhelm DC and knock out thrusters/radar panels, stunning anyone unfortunate enough to be shot by them. Unable to dodge and repair damage, ships in this state are very susceptible to 450 mm guns, even at max range. This type of fleet can deal with almost any other pure 450mm capital ship, forcing it to either abandon position and give space, or die if combined fire is intense enough. The key to this fleet being effective is keeping proper distance and protecting your main dmg dealing hull, the 450mm capital ship from being killed in frontline fight before the rail fire can take an effect.
**Counters**
Backline assets such are rail ships are usually weakly defended, they are prime target for missiles, cavalry flank or craft. Once the support rail assets are gone, such fleet loses its favorable matchup against other capital ships and is prone to being overwhelmed in head on fight.
**Balance changes**
Cheaper cruise S2H could encourage more frequent fishing for backline rails, but its not a significant change. If new MD frag shell is to be added, OSP version of this build could see ppl mixing in MDs into equation for more anti-light utility.

MD/rail counter battery (LRT has always greater range), well timed craft/rocket shuttle strike form behind cover, using cover to avoid rail fire.

**Fleet Archetype**
A carrier lineship (hereafter CVLN) which is equipped primarily for sortieing sturgeons with torpedoes. Typically very light on 'real' fighter assets or light strike in favor of overwhelmingly large presence with torpedoes.

**Why it's powerful**
It's hard to meaningfully oppose bombers without very proactive space superiority presence, especially when a CVLN likely has more sturgeons than your team has tantos. Meanwhile, said CVLN can bring ~30 individual sorties worth of torpedoes, typically in the area of 60 torpedoes.

Sturgeons themselves pose a threat to any target in the game in sufficient numbers. Torpedoes can leave even battleships on life support, and Sturgeons can deploy bombs to immediately DT break surviving components.

**Strategies for countering it**
SDM2s and S3H ACMs are both proactive measures that a ship can take for defending itself against bomber wings. Air superiority usually wins well against dedicated torp-sturgeon CVLNs since they necessarily spend very little on high end barracudas for airsup work. Past that, OSP only has access to radar, CMD, and wake seekers; omnisoftkill against their typical seeker ensemble followed by measures to avoid being hit by straightrunning CMD/SAH (or CMD/HOJ) torps can sometimes foil bomber strikes.

**Balance changes it's affected by**
The incoming PTB is going to severely reduce craft manueverability. This makes sturgeons far more vulnerable during their approach phase to conventional hardkill, while also featuring buffs to RPF's performance against craft. Thus, intercepting sturgeons before they can fire will become easier than it is on live.

The PTB also removes SDM2 from ANS, though the performance boost sarissa experienced likely makes up the difference, on-balance.
